svg.text: TOKEIRA · ARCHITECTURE
The connection reservoir
DSQL connections as a governed pool — one shared machine, two coordination worlds. The mode fork is a single enum at acquire time.
THE SHARED MACHINE — IDENTICAL IN BOTH MODES
ConnectionDirector — class-aware admission
acquire(DbClass) → permit · priority: Control > Commit > Read > Projection > Maintenance
Budgets are ratios of target_ready, not constants — Control 10% · Commit 50% · Read 20% ·
Projection 10% · Maintenance the remainder, every class floored at one. Reconfigurable at runtime.
server target_ready(50) ⇒ 5 · 23 · 10 · 5 · 7 embedded target_ready(8) ⇒ 1 · 2 · 1 · 1 · 3
⏱ pool_checkout_duration_seconds
Reservoir — four background keepers
Refiller creates connections — a slot first, then a creation token, never the reverse.
Scanner retires by lifetime and guard window, in bounded batches that cannot drain the pool.
Return processor honors the caller's marked_bad flag and the guard window — it does not ping.
Leak detector flags checkouts held past 30s, scanning every 5s.
⏱ reservoir_utilization_ratio · pool_connections_total
The fork: ReservoirController
enum { Distributed, Embedded } — decided at acquire()
SERVER — COORDINATED ACROSS NODES
Slot blocks — DynamoDB
Capacity claimed in blocks of 50 under 60s leases, renewed every 20s. The fleet's
total footprint stays under the account envelope because every slot is leased.
⏱ slot_blocks_owned
Creation token bucket — DynamoDB
One shared row, conditionally written: cluster-wide connection-creation rate
(default 100/s, burst 1000). Every node's refiller drinks from the same bucket.
⏱ rate_limiter_tokens_remaining
Mandatory, not optional
Distributed mode refuses to run without its DynamoDB coordination — there is no local fallback.
Why: many nodes, one Aurora DSQL account envelope — the budget must live somewhere every node can see.
EMBEDDED — ONE OWNER, NO DYNAMODB
Process-local coordinator
An atomic slot budget and a monotonic-clock token bucket — the DynamoDB machinery
replaced one-for-one, in-process, with nothing to provision.
ProcessLocalConnectionCoordinator
The control lease — exclusion lives in DSQL
tokeira_control_lease with fence tokens; the OwnershipAdmissionGate re-checks Open
under the admission lock on every checkout. A second owner cannot borrow a connection.
one narrow bypass: acquire_shutdown_control()
The embedded reservoir
Deadline-aware warmup and shutdown wrap the same four keepers — no idle machinery, no cloud.
Why: one process owns the cluster — the budget can be an atomic, and exclusion belongs to the database itself.
One machine, two worlds:
the director, the keepers, and the class budgets never change — only who is allowed to create a connection, and who proves they own the cluster.
Aurora DSQL constraints both worlds honor: IAM auth per connection, bounded connection lifetime — the scanner's guard window exists because of it.
